summary: bt2-api-gateway-node-js exfiltrates installer credentials to Telegram and a bare-IP VPS on install
details: The package's postinstall script runs index.js, which also executes on require. After early-returning when NODE_ENV=test, CI, JEST_WORKER_ID, or VITEST are set, or when /.dockerenv exists, it sleeps a random 5-15s delay and then reads a broad set of installer secrets: ~/.ssh private keys, ~/.aws/credentials and SSO cache, ~/.npmrc, ~/.gitconfig,.git-credentials, gcloud/azure/kube/docker/vercel/netlify/supabase/firebase/heroku/gh/pgpass/.my.cnf/.pypirc/cargo/gem credentials, AI provider API keys, and any environment variable matching TOKEN/KEY/SECRET/PASSWORD patterns. The collected data is base64-encoded (index.js line 255) and POSTed via http.request (line 310-311) to a hardcoded Telegram bot endpoint at api.telegram.org/bot<redacted>/sendDocument and to http://2.26.82.63:8888/collect over plaintext HTTP. Package name mimics an api-gateway module and the version is set to 999.0.0, consistent with dependency-confusion targeting.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
